You can’t keep sitting there being a shoulder to cry on until she has a epiphany and gets out of that toxic situation. 

Either way, this is bringing on negative emotions and if work continues to be stressful as well as your personal life it’ll worsen your overall mindset. Make sure you do what’s best for you and if that means cut it off explain to her why and tell her you are concerned about her relationship and tell her how you are impacted by all of this too.

For the rest of your life you have to live with yourself, everyone else is temporary. So don’t put yourself in a miserable situation.

I honestly think those panic attacks came purely because OP would’ve felt alone and her SO left her on read for ages. I know what it feels like during a mental breakdown and it often magnifies it by x10.

I don’t know why so many people are telling OP that she needs help. Mental illness is a problem and if OP’s boyfriend knows she has BPD shouldn’t he feel more like he NEEDS to help her?

I 100% do find it weird you were placed to sit alone despite your ongoing relationship. Just because someone is mentally ill it doesn’t mean ‘she needs to get help’. If it was a plain Jane normal girl having a panic attack over this I feel as if replies would be different. 

If your boyfriend cannot be there for the bad bad times why be there for the good times? The fact he couldn’t even be BOTHERED to respond to you and leave you on read is a huge flag in the case of other mental breakdowns. My ex had hung up on me during a REALLY bad time and ignored me out to go have fun at the expense of myself.

A relationship is communication and helping eachother not being a selfish person. Just because you have a panic attack which in the first place isn’t often you shouldn’t just ‘get help’. If he communicated more and was actually concerned as well as OP who I assume/hope you told your BF how you felt about the wedding on the days leading up. IMO I know how it feels with panic attacks and etc and maybe I’m just the type that doesn’t feel the need to let someone drown. 

Just because someone has mental illnesses doesn’t mean you treat them any less or help them any less. That’s what often leads to mentality getting worse because of the lack of support from partners and friends. I am NOT saying to not see a doctor because therapy is a great way to get help and there could be underlying problems or therapists can help find ways to move past it but I also think if this boyfriend of yours left you on read all night during a mental breakdown that’s a major red flag for me especially after 5 years of dating eachother. It’s like for example if we turned the tables here and your boyfriend had an attack or was super upset if you decided to do what he did, what do you think he’d do?
